title: Zeta research: what we tried and why
scope: Selected routes documented in the frozen 411-page main reader. The central object is the Riemann zeta function ζ(s), its completed function Xi(t)=ξ(1/2+it), and the Mellin transform (an integral transform that records power-law coefficients as a function of the complex variable s) and heat transforms acting on them. The reader also studies CUE characteristic-polynomial moments; CUE means the circular unitary ensemble, the probability model of Haar-random unitary matrices. The geometric and fluid models are written explicitly; this is not an exhaustive account of the literature corpus or every sidebar.
overall_aim: Reconstruct published results about the Riemann zeta function and connect them, by explicit formulas rather than metaphor, to three named inputs: the CUE (circular unitary ensemble) characteristic-polynomial literature; the cubic polynomial map F:C^3→C^3 discussed by Tao, Speyer and Poplett; and the corrected finite-time Navier–Stokes reconstruction published as a companion reader. The broader motivation was to determine exactly what arithmetic information these interfaces carry and whether any route reaches a criterion relevant to the Riemann hypothesis (RH).

context.zeta_object: ζ(s) is the Riemann zeta function; Xi(t)=ξ(1/2+it) is the completed zeta function evaluated on the critical-line coordinate s=1/2+it. The arithmetic multiplier used in the fluid routes is W_h(s)=ζ(s)(1−2^{s−1})(1−2^{h−s}), for the stated parameter h.
context.cue_object: The random-matrix input is the CUE characteristic polynomial det(I−zU) of a Haar-random unitary matrix U and its derivative moments, sourced to A. Grover, F. Mezzadri and N. Simm, Higher order derivative moments of CUE characteristic polynomials and the Riemann zeta function, arXiv:2604.03051v1, plus the Easy Riders public channel supplied by the user.
context.geometric_object: The geometric input is the explicitly written cubic map F=(F1,F2,F3):C^3→C^3 with F1=(1+xy)^3w+y^2(1+xy)(4+3xy), F2=y+3x(1+xy)^2w+3xy^2(4+3xy), and F3=2x−3x^2y−x^3w. The reader attributes the displayed map and explanations to Terry Tao, David Speyer and J. Poplett; it is not an unspecified 'supplied polynomial'.
context.fluid_object: The fluid input is the corrected 208-page Finite Time Blowup for Navier–Stokes reconstruction, with positive viscosity ν>0, zero initial velocity, smooth compactly supported forcing, pressure and nonlinear transport retained. The public companion edition is archived at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22678406; the reader records its source attribution and says independent analytical/Lean validation remains unfinished.
context.relation_policy: The entries below say which map or transform was actually used. A typed construction means that its domain, codomain and formula are stated. They do not identify ζ, a CUE polynomial, F, or the fluid field as the same object; any relation claimed is the displayed typed construction and its stated scope.

motivation_policy: The broad motivation follows the owner's stated research direction. The short route rationales below are reconstructed from the written arguments, not claimed as verbatim historical statements of intent.
evidence_policy: These are descriptive accounts of existing written calculations and recorded checks. This editorial pass reads the cited passages and verifies artifact identity; it does not rerun the mathematical computations or independently replay the imported Navier–Stokes existence theorem. Incomplete means incomplete in the cited work, not unknown throughout mathematics.

attempts.title: Keep the branches, then transport the equations
attempts.aim: Test whether the explicit Tao–Speyer–Poplett cubic map can be carried into fluid and arithmetic coordinates without losing inverse branches.
attempts.why_it_looked_promising: An inverse fibre is the set of input points with one fixed output under F, so its geometry gives a concrete place to calculate exactly what a projection forgets.
attempts.tried: Started from the displayed F1,F2,F3 formulas and constructed the cubic inverse chart, rank-degenerate exceptional fibres, incompressible trajectories and diffusion operators after changing coordinates.
attempts.outcome: Obtained exact maps and an escaping trajectory in the retained pullback metric.
attempts.extent_and_unfinished: That metric is incomplete; this route did not itself produce a classical Euclidean Navier–Stokes singularity or an off-critical zeta zero. The later work therefore also uses the actual released fluid field.

attempts.title: Test the negative coefficient in the complete Weil form
attempts.aim: Determine whether the coefficient-level negative signal survives in a quadratic Weil-form test relevant to RH. The Weil form here is the explicit quadratic functional used in a Weil-type positivity criterion.
attempts.why_it_looked_promising: The retained coefficient acts on the actual theta input (a Gaussian-weighted theta series) whose Fourier transform is Xi.
attempts.tried: Evaluated the complete Weil form, retaining pole, gamma and prime-power terms, cross terms and infinite-tail bounds.
attempts.outcome: The recorded certified value is positive, approximately 2.0984855607004 × 10⁻¹¹.
attempts.extent_and_unfinished: This particular input is not a negative Weil witness. The calculation neither proves global Weil positivity nor settles RH; the negative linear coefficient remains a different, explicitly related calculation.

attempts.title: Transport the actual concentrating swirl into arithmetic
attempts.aim: Propagate the corrected Navier–Stokes reconstruction's actual velocity and angular momentum into zeta Mellin coordinates (integral coordinates indexed by the complex exponent s), rather than infer its behaviour from an analogy.
attempts.why_it_looked_promising: The published construction has an explicitly defined concentrating component, while angular momentum admits explicit dilation and Mellin maps involving ζ(s).
attempts.tried: Kept the named field uν, pressure, force, positive viscosity, both nonlinear fluxes and the projection remainder; constructed the arithmetic map and inverse, then examined the fixed-axis derivative.
attempts.outcome: The written calculation obtains a directly growing arithmetic derivative and an equal genuine Mellin residue at s = −1.
attempts.extent_and_unfinished: This is a precise transported signal, not an off-critical zeta zero. Independent verification of the imported complete source existence theorem is unfinished.

attempts.title: Recover data hidden by trivial-zero cancellation
attempts.aim: Find where higher radial information goes when a zeta factor cancels its Mellin pole. The cancellation occurs at the zeta factor's trivial zeros (the negative even integers).
attempts.why_it_looked_promising: A cancelled pole need not mean that the input coefficient has disappeared.
attempts.tried: Expanded the full Mellin product at negative integers and retained the local zeta factors.
attempts.outcome: Odd Taylor coefficients are recovered from residues; even coefficients from regular values divided by the nonzero derivative of the multiplier.
attempts.extent_and_unfinished: This recovers the complete Taylor sequence, not an arbitrary smooth germ from that sequence alone. Flat remainders (nonzero functions invisible to every Taylor coefficient at the expansion point) remain in the full invertible transform; no new nontrivial zeta zero is obtained.

attempts.title: Make the higher radial source data constructive
attempts.aim: Extend the axis calculation beyond its first derivative without replacing the complete corrected field.
attempts.why_it_looked_promising: The preceding second-coefficient cancellation suggested finite source dependence at each fixed radial degree.
attempts.tried: Derived the coupled coefficient recursion (a recurrence determining the next radial coefficient from earlier ones) with pressure, viscosity and cutoff terms, then carried it into residue/value coordinates.
attempts.outcome: The written induction gives vanishing above correction order n > m and a finite algorithm for every fixed Taylor degree.
attempts.extent_and_unfinished: This is not convergence of the uncut series or an autonomous finite-dimensional fluid system. The full functions, nonlinear fluxes and flat remainders remain necessary.
